item.title: Kennedy Chandler's Surprising NBA Comeback: From G League Assists Leader to Jazz Starter
item.description:
What does it take to go from averaging 7.8 minutes per game as a rookie to dropping a career-high 31 points in just three seasons? For Kennedy Chandler, the answer was a detour through the G League — and a relentless refusal to let his NBA dream die.

Key Takeaways:

  • Kennedy Chandler signed two consecutive 10-day contracts with the Utah Jazz after dominating the G League
  • He averaged 12.0 points, 6.2 assists, and 2.8 rebounds in 30.1 minutes across nine games with Utah
  • Chandler exploded for a career-high 31 points, 8 assists, and 7 rebounds in the Jazz’s season finale
  • The former 38th overall pick in 2022 is now a serious contender for a full-time NBA roster spot

Kennedy Chandler’s Road Back to the NBA

The 23-year-old point guard’s NBA journey has been anything but linear. Selected as the 38th overall pick in the 2022 NBA Draft by the Memphis Grizzlies, Chandler’s rookie season offered only a brief glimpse of his potential. In 33 regular season games during the 2022-23 campaign, he averaged just 2.2 points, 1.6 assists, and 1.1 rebounds in 7.8 minutes per game, shooting 42.2% from the field.

item.title: Drew Timme's Surprising Rise: From Undrafted to Lakers Starter
item.description:
Drew Timme’s Surprising Rise: From Undrafted to Lakers Starter

Gonzaga’s all-time leading scorer couldn’t get drafted. Now Drew Timme is starting games for the Los Angeles Lakers — and making believers out of everyone who counted him out.

Key Takeaways:

  • Drew Timme signed a two-way contract with the Lakers in November 2025 after Deandre Ayton’s injury
  • The 25-year-old averaged 25.5 points, 7.5 rebounds, and 4.0 assists with the South Bay Lakers in the G League
  • As Gonzaga’s all-time leading scorer (2,307 points), Timme went undrafted in 2023 before grinding through the G League
  • He’s now earning starts for the Lakers, including an April 8 matchup against OKC

From March Madness Star to Undrafted Free Agent

Drew Timme wasn’t supposed to end up here. At Gonzaga, the 6-foot-10 big man was a three-time All-American and two-time West Coast Conference Player of the Year. He left as the program’s all-time leading scorer with 2,307 points across four seasons — a resume that screams NBA lottery pick in most eras.
